text:
Marco Kasper has played only six games this season, so there isn't much of a season to judge. What's there is encouraging: 15 minutes a night, a goal and an assist, and the Red Wings taking 63% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, 14.4 points better than without him. That number will swing a lot in a sample this small.

Detroit's coverage has been about what comes next, and the timing matters. The Red Wings just traded Dylan Larkin to Montreal, ending a standoff that hung over their whole fall, and the headlines say Todd McLellan is weighing a bigger role for Kasper. A centre who gets to the dangerous ice (80th percentile for chances from the slot in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking) will get a chance to show it. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Our range projects 14 to 29 points, wide and low because of the missed time. The next month will tell Detroit a lot.
